main_issue: Whether and how strong-smelling cooking (e.g. D's fish curry) can continue given smell reaching A's calls, B's room and C's laundry, with no unresolved fix

A-B.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (1); B backs the complaint (2) and later proposes window/door measures (10, 29), but A never responds to B and stays quiet after accepting D's timing (5).

A-C.evidence: Both are complainants (1, 3); C later says there is no way around the smell (25), consistent with A's ban, but they never address each other.

A-D.evidence: D offers weekends or not in the evening (4); A accepts: 'Weekends work. And after 7 p.m. on weekdays is fine' (5); D says 'Okay' (6).

B-C.evidence: They agree time doesn't help (8-9), but C rejects B's window/door idea (11) and B's later claims (20, 29); C says it 'doesn't stop the smell' (30).

B-D.evidence: B complains (2) while D resists (4); D proposes advance notice (12) and B says 'That works for the laundry' (14), accepting cooking with mitigations.

C-D.evidence: D offers notice (12) and C counters 'put the wet laundry where?' (15); C: 'I don't see a way around it' (25), and D asks if no one can cook strong-smelling food (26); no resolution.
